newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kinkel says Germany against weakening EMU criteria.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel says Germany against weakening EMU criteria.

text.p: Foreign Minsiter Klaus Kinkel on Wednesday repeated Germany's tough line on sticking to the strict fiscal criteria for Europe's planned single currency and ruled out any delay in economic and monetary union (EMU).

Any delay in the single currency, planned for 1999, or weakening of the fiscal targets outlined in the Maastricht Treaty on EMU would hurt acceptance of the currency on financial markets and by European citizens, he said.
Kinkel says Germany against weakening EMU criteria

"The euro must, as agreed in Maastricht, come on January 1, 1999. A delay is not an option, and any softening of the criteria is out of the question," the minister said in a statement after a special meeting of the federal cabinet.

The cabinet met to discuss European affairs before the European Union (EU) summit in Dublin next week. Kinkel said it was necessary to "close the holes" in the Maastricht Treaty and appealed for agreement on an EMU stability pact.
"Monetary union is only conceivable as a community of stability," he said. "Therefore, we must back up budget discipline in the EU member states with a stability pact."
Kinkel added that Germany and France would outline the details of a joint initiative on EMU at the Franco-German summit next week, before the Dublin conference.
